messages.author: cc5ff254a0864dd8
messages.subject: GeneActiv Lux Output
parts:
Hello! I wanted to ask if there is code I could add to my GGIR script that would give me epoch-by-epoch lux measurements? We use the newest generation of GeneActiv watches.
Thank you so much, 
Michelle

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] GeneActiv Lux Output
parts:
Hi Michelle,

For GENEActiv, this is part of the part5 time series output.
See documentation for arguments:
-   save_ms5rawlevels
-   save_ms5raw_format
-   save_ms5raw_without_invalid

https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/GGIRParameters.html
You could consider reducing the long epoch length in part 1 (default 15 minutes), e.g. to 300 seconds, to get higher resolution LUX in part 5.

Best, Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

library(GGIR)
library(GGIRread)
GGIR(mode=c(1,2,3,4,5),
     datadir="C:/Users/u1370752/Box/KINES Depner Lab/MASTER LAB Folder/Studies/TOCS/Analyses and Data/Actigraphy/Data",

     do.report=c(2,4,5),
     overwrite = TRUE,
     windowsizes = c(5,900,3600),
     do.cal = TRUE,
     do.enmo = TRUE,             do.anglez=TRUE,

     idloc=1,

     timethreshold= 5,        anglethreshold=5,
     ignorenonwear = TRUE,
     outliers.only = FALSE,
     criterror = 4,
     do.visual = TRUE,
     #=====================
     # Part 5
     #=====================
     threshold.lig = c(30), threshold.mod = c(100),  threshold.vig = c(400),
     boutcriter = 0.8,      boutcriter.in = 0.9,     boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
     boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8, boutdur.in = c(1,10,30), boutdur.lig = c(1,10),
     boutdur.mvpa = c(1),
     includedaycrit.part5 = 2/3,
     save.ms5rawlevels = TRUE,
     save.ms5raw.format = "csv",
     save.ms5raw.without.invalid = FALSE,
     #=====================
     # Visual report
     #=====================
     timewindow = c("WW"),
     visualreport=TRUE)

messages.author: e0169f921473cc94
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] GeneActiv Lux Output
parts:
Misia,

The epoch-by-epoch output, which includes a lightpeak column with lux values, is located in /output_folder/meta/ms5.outraw

In that folder you'll find a "behavioralcodes" CSV file and then another folder (I think the name depends upon activity thresholds) that contains 1 epoch-by-epoch CSV per recording.

Importantly, I think you need to fix your ms5-related configuration options to use an underscore (e.g., save_ms5rawlevels) instead of a period (e.g., save.ms5rawlevels in your code snippet above).

Hope that helps!

Note that for the new GENEActiv 1.2 model ActivInsights has informed me that the lux values have a different non-linear output coding. I have a few test recordings for which the light peak values seem plausible, so this is not easy to spot.

Best regards,

Vincent
